title: Field Upgrade Dry‑Run and Evidence Bundle Template
author: Sofia Patel
summary: A prescriptive dry‑run framework for private (VPC/on‑prem) upgrades that standardizes operator activities, telemetry capture, and an evidence bundle for customer-observed cutovers and forensic rollbacks.
content:
Purpose and scope

This document defines a repeatable field upgrade dry‑run procedure and an evidence bundle template used for private deployments (VPC and on‑prem). It is intended for operator teams executing witnessed cutovers, acceptance testing with customer sites, and for any rollback forensic needs. The playbook covers:

- preflight checks and acceptance criteria
- deterministic workload & smoke tests to run during the dry run
- telemetry and artifact capture (evidence bundle format)
- abort and rollback criteria with operator commands
- signoff and audit steps

Audience

- Field Operators
- Site Reliability Engineers (SRE) supporting private deployments
- Customer Technical Contacts during witnessed upgrades

Owner and contact

- Owner: Eng - Private Deployments (upgrade-and-rollback)
- Primary oncall: private-deploy-oncall@redwood.internal
- Escalation: Head of Field Ops — Marco Rossi

Definitions and constraints

- Dry‑run: A full upgrade rehearsal on production‑like tenant(s) or a short window on low‑impact tenants intended to validate process, not to change customer-facing state permanently.
- Evidence bundle: A time‑boxed tarball containing logs, checksums, manifests and signed attestations produced by the operator and uploaded to the evidence store.
- Timebox: Default dry‑run window is 90 minutes. Extensions require explicit approval from the customer and Eng manager.

Acceptance criteria (preflight)

Operators must confirm the following before the dry run begins:

1. Tickets and approvals: Signed change request present and customer acceptance window scheduled.
2. Backups & snapshots: Model artifacts snapshot, KV cache snapshot (if supported) and control plane metadata backed up to S3-compatible store.

- Backup retention: Keep for 72 hours unless customer requires longer.
- Snapshot tags: "dryrun-<YYYYMMDD>-<operator>".

3. Metrics baseline captured: 24h rolling baseline for p50/p95/p99 latency, error rate, and throughput.

4. Operator readiness checklist: Red team, runbook, and rollback owner assigned.

Preflight checklist (short)

- Verify operator SSH keys and KMS access (kms-key-id).
- Confirm image digests and signed artifacts: sha256 of runtime and model artifacts.
- Ensure telemetry sampling is set to 100% for the dry‑run tenants.

Dry‑run timeline (recommended)

| Phase | Duration | Owner | Outcome |
|---|---:|---|---|
| Preflight validation | 15m | Operator | Baseline snapshot & checklist complete |
| Staged rollout step (canary) | 20m | Operator | Canary tenants upgraded, smoke tests green |
| Functional smoke & load tests | 30m | Test lead | Performance within thresholds |
| Evidence capture & packaging | 15m | Operator | Evidence bundle created and uploaded |
| Signoff & rollback window | 10m | Customer + Operator | Final acceptance or rollback decision |
Total: ~90 minutes

Deterministic smoke and acceptance tests

Follow this ordered list during the test window:

1. Sanity checks (immediate): connectivity to model endpoints, auth, and KMS operations.
2. Warmup sequence: 10 canonical prompts to ensure KV cache warmup; record cold vs warm token latency.
3. Canary RPS load: Ramp to 20% of production observed baseline for the selected tenant; measure p95 latency.
4. Quantized path validation: If the upgrade includes new quantized kernels, run a correctness test set of 100 labeled prompts and compute BLEU/ROUGE/semantic similarity regression thresholds.
5. Failure injection (optional): Network tail-loss simulation for 30s on a non-production tenant to validate graceful degradation.

Pass/fail thresholds (defaults)

- Latency: p95 <= baseline_p95 * 1.15 and p99 <= baseline_p99 * 1.25
- Error rate: increase <= 0.2 percentage points absolute
- Model correctness: semantic-similarity decline <= 2% on golden prompt set

Abort conditions (immediate stop)

- sustained p99 latency > baseline_p99 * 1.5 for > 2 minutes
- error rate spike > +1.0 percentage points absolute
- asset checksum mismatch for deployed artifacts

Evidence bundle schema (flat file layout)

The evidence bundle is a gzipped tar (tar.gz) with the following top-level layout. Operators must populate each file and avoid nested JSON objects inside manifest files (use flat key-value lines). Example structure:

evidence-<tenant>-<YYYYMMDD>-<operator>.tar.gz
|-- manifest.txt                # flat key=value lines (see template below)
|-- artifacts/
|   |-- runtime-image.sha256     # single-line sha256sum
|   |-- model-weights.sha256     # single-line sha256sum
|-- logs/
|   |-- operator-console.log    # full operator console output
|   |-- upgrade-steps.log        # step-by-step execution log with timestamps
|-- metrics/
|   |-- baseline-metrics.csv    # CSV: timestamp,metric,value
|   |-- dryrun-metrics.csv       # CSV matching the same schema
|-- telemetry-samples.jsonl      # line-delimited JSON events (max 10000 lines)
|-- signatures/
|   |-- operator.sig             # operator GPG signature of manifest.txt
|   |-- customer-witness.sig     # customer-signed acceptance (optional)

manifest.txt template (required keys)

operator=sofia.patel@redwood.internal
customer=acme-corp
tenant=acme-prod-3
start_time=2026-02-20T14:05:00Z
end_time=2026-02-20T15:35:00Z
runtime_image_digest=sha256:xxxxxxxx
model_weights_digest=sha256:yyyyyyyy
backup_location=s3://redwood-evidence/dryruns/acme-prod-3/
baseline_p95=120ms
dryrun_p95=130ms
abort_trigger=none
notes=Canary succeeded, observed 4% CPU rise on host-n6

Operator commands and snippets (examples)

- Create snapshot (example):
  aws s3 cp s3://backups/model-weights-20260215.tar.gz s3://redwood-evidence/dryruns/ --profile field-ops

- Compute sha256 (Linux):
  sha256sum model-weights.tgz > model-weights.sha256

- Collect metrics (prometheus query, CSV export):
  ./prom-csv-export --query='histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(http_request_duration_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le))' --from=2026-02-19T14:00:00Z --to=2026-02-20T14:00:00Z > baseline-metrics.csv

- Create evidence tarball:
  tar -czf evidence-acme-prod-3-20260220.tgz manifest.txt artifacts/ logs/ metrics/ telemetry-samples.jsonl signatures/

- Sign manifest with GPG (operator):
  gpg --armor --output signatures/operator.sig --detach-sig manifest.txt

Uploading and retention

- Primary upload target: s3://redwood-evidence/dryruns/<tenant>/<evidence-id>/
- Secondary: customer-provided secure FTP or RDC if required by contract (document location in manifest).
- Retention default: 90 days for dry runs unless customer requests longer retention.

Rollback quick reference (if dry‑run uncovered regressions)

1. Halt further rollout: set operator flag rollouts.enabled=false in control plane (kubectl patch or API).
2. Redispatch previous artifacts: use artifact digests recorded in manifest to redeploy previous runtime and model snapshot. Example CLI: 
   redwoodctl deploy --tenant acme-prod-3 --image sha256:xxxxxxxx --model-weights s3://backups/model-weights-20260214.tgz --force-restart
3. Validate KV cache consistency: run kv-checksum script and compare to backup snapshot.
4. Reopen observation window for 30m and verify metrics return to baseline.

Post‑dry‑run audit and signoff

- Within 24 hours the operator must:
  - Upload the evidence bundle and manifest and notify customer + SRE oncall.
  - Fill in the postmortem template if any aborts or unexpected results occurred.
  - Record lessons learned and update the runbook for next iteration.

- Acceptance signoff form (flat text appended to manifest.txt):
  operator_accept=sofia.patel@redwood.internal
  operator_accept_time=2026-02-20T16:00:00Z
  customer_witnessed=true
  customer_signoff=alice.jensen@acme-corp

Automations and test harnesses

- Integrate this playbook with the dry‑run harness located in repo: git@internal:redwood/ops/dryrun-harness.git. The harness supports automated metric collection, CSV exports, and evidence bundle assembly.

- Recommended CI check: the harness must validate that manifest.txt contains all required keys before allowing tar creation.

Related pages

- Reference: private-deploy-evidence-preservation-and-forensic-playbook-2026 (see upgrade-and-rollback)
- Operator training: operator-onboarding-kickstart-and-telemetry-contract-2026

Change log

- 2026-02-15: First published (Sofia Patel).
- 2026-03-01: Clarified evidence manifest required keys and tightened default retention to 90 days.

Appendix: Troubleshooting quick hits

- If telemetry-samples.jsonl is >10k lines, split into telemetry-samples-1.jsonl, telemetry-samples-2.jsonl and list both in manifest.
- If GPG signing fails due to missing key, use operator emergency signing procedure (see key-recovery-runbook under security-and-compliance).

End of document
